# `Q-5-26` — Alias Resolves Outside the Output Directory

> An `aliases:` entry climbs above the site's output directory.
> Redirect stubs must be written inside the site.

## What this means

A redirect stub is a file in your site's output directory. An
alias with enough `../` segments to climb out of it would write
somewhere else on disk — outside the site, and outside anything
you would deploy.

```yaml
---
title: Deployment
aliases:
  - ../../old-site/deploy.html   # above the output directory
---
```

## Why this happens

Relative aliases resolve against the **page's own output
location**, not against the project root. A page that renders deep
in the tree can climb further than its author expected:

```yaml
# renders to _site/index.html
aliases:
  - ../old.html    # one level above _site/ — rejected
```

Absolute aliases have the same limit: a leading `/` means the root
of the site, so `/../old.html` also climbs out.

## How to fix it

Use a site-root-relative alias, which is almost always what is
meant:

```yaml
aliases:
  - /old.html      # _site/old.html
```

If you need to redirect from a URL your Quarto project does not
build, that redirect belongs in your web server or hosting
configuration rather than in `aliases:`.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 has no guard here and will write the file wherever the
path lands.
